title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior 5%+ price hikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) averaged x0.57 vs baseline; 5.1% increase suggests similar drop. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk to x0.74.

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: Store closed one day (1/7); average daily sales ~29.7 units; 14.3% reduction in weekly volume.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. The store is closed Monday (1/7 of week), reducing demand. Price is up 5.1% (4.56 vs 4.34), a known demand reducer. Past price hikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show ~25% drop vs baseline. The 2026-10-05 week had 119 units (x0.57), aligning with a 5% price increase. A 5.1% increase implies a similar or slightly smaller drop. No promotion, event, or seasonal ramp. The classical model is silent, but we have direct evidence. Adjust down for price and closure. Evidence is strong, but no prior 5.1% increase, so shrink toward 1.0. Median adjusted down to 0.74. Spread widens slightly due to price effect uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.2 - 290.7 | 10%-90%: 156.0 - 281.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
